title: The address to the traditions' expectations
statement: In the second message's closing address, Yahweh calls each tradition to recognize its own expectation in the present message: the Christian who has read 'a hundred times that Jesus would return' (ETTMTTP-3:226), the child of Israel who 'still waits for your messiah' (3:227), the Buddhist whose 'writings indicate that the new Buddha must be born in the West; recognize the foreseen signs!' (3:228), and the Muslim told to 'welcome the last of the prophets' (3:229); read in that context and with ETTMTTP-3:257, where Raël is 'the last of the line of the prophets', the corpus takes the Buddhist clause as pointing at Raël, carried in the canon's own words.

includes: The parallel address structure of ETTMTTP-3:226–229, quoted in the canon's own words
The contextual inference: the Buddhist clause, read with its neighbours and with ETTMTTP-3:257, points at Raël
The inference's grade: only the Muslim clause names 'the last of the prophets'; the Buddhist clause points by parallel, which is why the label is inferred
excludes: The name Maitreya (Metteyya) and any identification of the canon's 'new Buddha' with the Maitreya of Buddhist tradition (founder direction, 2026-11-08)
Any claim that Buddhist scriptures in fact predict a birth in the West; the record carries what the canon says the writings indicate, not what they say
Raël's later titles and publications (post-canon reception), which this record does not use
Any re-description of the other traditions' expectations beyond the address's own words

source_references.locator: ETTMTTP-3:226–229 (the address to Christian, child of Israel, Buddhist, Muslim); ETTMTTP-3:257 ('the last of the line of the prophets')
Reference treatment of the Buddhist future-buddha tradition — the comparative control against which the canon's 'born in the West' clause is checked

alternatives.statement: The classical Buddhist accounts of the next buddha are generally reported to place him in India in a remote future age, not in the West; if so, the canon's clause characterizes the Buddhist writings in a way the writings do not bear out (primary-text check outstanding).
ETTMTTP-3:226–229 is exhortation addressed to readers of each tradition, not a doctrine of identification; reading a designation of Raël out of the Buddhist clause over-reads rhetoric.

revision_triggers: A primary-text check of the Buddhist future-buddha sources confirms or refutes the 'born in the West' characterization.
Claim woh-claim-0038 or woh-claim-0077 is revised or retired.
Public prose begins naming Maitreya or asserting what Buddhist scripture predicts, both of which this record excludes.
